sentences.text: Today, we will talk about Montenegro.
Montenegro is a small, beautiful, and peaceful country in southeastern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Montenegro?
Montenegro is in Europe, on the Balkan Peninsula.
It is next to Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Kosovo, and Albania.
To the west, it has a coast on the Adriatic Sea.
Montenegro has mountains, rivers, and sea views.
What is the capital city of Montenegro?
The capital city is Podgorica.
It is the largest city in the country.
It has parks, bridges, and modern buildings.
Other important places include Kotor, a beautiful old town by the sea.
Budva, known for beaches and nightlife.
Satinja, a historic royal town.
Herzegnovi, a lovely town near the Croatian border.
How many people live in Montenegro?
About 600,000 people live in Montenegro.
It is a small country with a low population.
Most people live in towns and cities along the coast or in the valleys.
What language do people speak in Montenegro?
The official language is Montenegren.
Many people also speak Serbian Bosnian, Croatian, Albanian.
English is taught in schools and spoken in tourist areas.
What is the weather like in Montenegro?
Montenegro has two main climates.
On the coast, the weather is Mediterranean.
Hot summers and mild winters.
In the mountains, the weather is colder with snow and winter.
Summers are perfect for beach trips and winters are good for skiing.
What does Montenegro look like?
Montenegro has high mountains and deep canyons, clear rivers and green forests, old towns with stone houses, beautiful beaches by the Adriatic Sea, Lake Skadar, the biggest lake in the Balkans.
It is a country full of natural beauty and historic places.
What animals live in Montenegro?
In Montenegro, you can find bears, wolves and foxes in the forests, eagles, owls and pelicans, fish, frogs and snakes in rivers and lakes, sheep, goats and cows on farms.
Nature is clean and protected in many areas.
What do people eat in Montenegro?
Montenegro and food is fresh, hearty and influenced by neighbors.

People eat bread, cheese and meat, fish, potatoes and vegetables, olives, fruit and honey, popular dishes, chivapi, small grilled meat sausages, burrek, pastry with meat, cheese or spinach, kachamak, cornmeal with cheese and cream, fish soup by the coast, prosciutto smoked ham like prosciutto drink in Montenegro.
People drink water often from natural springs, coffee strong and served in small cups, herbal tea, fruit juice.
Adults may drink rakia, a strong fruit brandy or local wine.
Coffee is part of everyday social life.
What is life like in Montenegro?
Life is peaceful, slow and family focused.
People enjoy walking by the sea, eating with family, talking with friends in cafes, celebrating holidays, spending time in nature.
People are proud of their land, traditions and hospitality.
What are some holidays and traditions in Montenegro?
Independence Day, May 21st.
Statehood Day, July 13th.
Christmas, January 7th Orthodox calendar.
Easter, a big holiday with red eggs.
Carnival and couture with music and costumes.
Many people go to church, make traditional food and visit family.
Some fun facts about Montenegro.
The name Montenegro means Black Mountain.
The Bay of Couture is one of the most beautiful bays in Europe.
Montenegro became independent in 2006.
It uses the Euro as its currency, but is not in the EU.
The Dermatur National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Now you know many things about Montenegro.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about the land, the people and daily life.
Great job.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
